name: Global Innovation Index: Puerto Rico profile (gii_profile.json)
plain: FPR's 2021 Global Innovation Index profile of Puerto Rico, kept as printed, with the newest open value of each indicator that can be updated, an arrow that says whether it is better or worse than in 2021 on the GII's scale, the indicator's status in the GII 2026 and, where the sources match, an indicative position among the GII 2026 economies. FPR's calculation, not an official ranking.
definition: One record for each of the 80 indicators of the GII 2020 framework (7 pillars, 21 sub-pillars), with the fields gii.*: the 2021 value, rank and marks (frozen), the updated value with its year, source and kind, and the GII 2026 comparison. The pillars block holds the names and descriptions; the texts block holds each indicator's name, definition, FPR method note, corrections and reason for no update, in English and Spanish; the sources block names the update sources; about counts the updated and compared indicators.
geography: Puerto Rico: the 80 indicators of the Global Innovation Index profile

coverage.frequency: The 2021 values are frozen; gii.py rebuilds the updated values and the GII 2026 comparison when FPR updates the page.

method: docs/analysis/gii-2021/gii_original.json is the profile frozen as printed (written once on 2026-10-23); gii.py reads it, fetches the open series (World Bank WGI and WDI, UNESCO UIS, IMF, BLS LAUS and OEWS, US EIA, Census Bureau population estimates; none needs an API key) into cache/gii/, takes the freshest candidate of each, and places the updated value among the GII 2026 economies for the indicators whose source and definition match.
how_to_read: Read the 2021 value and rank together. The updated value is not ranked among the GII 2020 economies; its arrow compares it with the 2021 value in the direction of the index. A position X/N among the GII 2026 economies is indicative. No overall, sub-index or pillar score exists for Puerto Rico.
caveats: Puerto Rico is not in the official Global Innovation Index; the ranks are FPR's.
The printed ranks are out of 132 even where fewer economies had data (rank_n).
Proprietary 2021 values (IHS Markit, Web of Science, Brand Finance) are not updated.
Sources revise past years (WGI, UIS, IMF), so an updated value is not a change from the printed one.

name: Indicative position among the GII 2026 economies
plain: Where Puerto Rico's updated value would fall among the GII 2026 economies with data, written c26_pos/c26_of like the profile's ranks. Indicative position calculated by FPR, not an official WIPO rank.
definition: c26_pos = 1 + the number of GII 2026 economies whose screened value is strictly better than Puerto Rico's (lower is better where c26_lower_better), so ties share the better place, as WIPO's own ranks do (true for 78 of the 79 indicators of the GII 2026 database); c26_of = the economies with data + 1. Ranking the value gives the place the 0-100 score would give, because min-max and the log transform keep the order; no position is given where the GII winsorizes and Puerto Rico's value lies beyond the capped values. For the 10 indicators whose Puerto Rico source and definition match (COMPARE in gii.py): 1.1.2, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 2.1.1, 2.1.3, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 3.2.3 and 4.3.3. 2.1.5, 4.3.1, 6.2.1 and 6.2.2 get none (NO_POSITION gives the reason in each open row).
unit: rank of the economies with data plus Puerto Rico

name: Direction of the indicator (GII scale)
plain: +1 when a higher value is a better outcome on the GII's scale, -1 when it is worse (the indicators marked *). It sets the colour of the change arrow; it follows the index's method, not a value judgement.
definition: -1 for 1.1.1, 1.2.3, 2.1.5 and 4.3.1, the indicators the GII 2020 Appendix III marks as 'higher values indicate worse outcomes' (the profile's *); +1 for the other 76. Checked in the data: in the GII 2020 values of FPR's working file and in the GII 2026 database, the score falls as the value rises for exactly these indicators (Spearman rank correlation below -0.97); the GII 2026 adds two new ones, 3.2.2 (aviation dwell time) and 4.3.2 (industry concentration).

name: Change marker of the updated value
plain: How the updated value compares with the printed 2021 value on the GII's scale: better (green arrow), worse (red arrow), no meaningful change (≈) or not comparable (—). 'Better' follows the index's direction, not a value judgement.
definition: chg = 'same' when |upd_value - value| < chg_thr, the threshold: 5% of the interquartile range (inclusive quartiles) of the GII 2026 economies' values for the matching indicator (on the GII's log scale, ln[(max - 1)(x - min)/(max - min) + 1], for the indicators the GII log-transforms: chg_log); otherwise 'better' when (upd_value - value) x dir > 0, else 'worse'. chg = 'na' when the profile has no 2021 value (chg_why 'no_2021', 2.2.3), the two were measured with different sources and definitions (chg_why 'definition': 6.2.1, whose original used the Junta de Planificación's fiscal-year GDP and which the GII 2026 redefined as a five-year average, and 6.2.2), or the source's series changed (chg_why 'series': 2.1.5, UIS's 2024 teacher series), or the method differs from FPR's 2021 one (chg_why 'method': 5.1.1, whose 2021 list of occupations is in FPR's working file, not in the repository; the SOC major groups used now give 29.6% for May 2019 and 30.2% for May 2020, not the printed 32.0). For the WGI (1.1.2, 1.2.1, 1.2.2), whose every release revises all past years, the base is the current release's value for 2018, the data year of the GII 2020 (its Appendix III), not the printed value: chg_base and chg_base_year; the printed value stays as published. chg_delta = upd_value - value (or - chg_base). The arrow points up or down with chg_delta; only the arrow is coloured, and it carries the words as its accessible label.

name: Status of the indicator in the GII 2026
plain: What became of the GII 2020 indicator in the latest edition, the GII 2026: same, renamed, redefined or dropped, with the GII 2026 code it maps to (c26_full).
definition: same: the same concept and definition, perhaps under a new code (49); renamed: the same concept with a new name or data provider (8); redefined: the definition or calculation changed (7: 3.1.1, 3.1.2, 4.2.3, 6.1.2, 6.2.1, 7.3.1 and 7.3.2, the last two merged into one); dropped: not in the GII 2026 (16). c26_full is the GII 2026 database code (IN.x.x.x or OUT.x.x.x). Curated in docs/analysis/gii-2021/gii_crosswalk.json from WIPO's GII 2026 database, its Appendix I and the GII 2025 Appendix I (checked 2026-10-23).

name: Global Innovation Index: changes since 2020 (gii_changes.json)
plain: What changed in the Global Innovation Index between the GII 2020, the method of FPR's 2021 profile, and the GII 2026: the editions, the method, the indicators that changed and the new ones, with whether Puerto Rico data exist.
definition: editions: economies, indicators, pillars and sub-pillars of the GII 2020, 2025 and 2026, each with its source; method: the changes in normalization, outlier treatment, weights, coverage, ranks and direction, in English and Spanish, each with its source; crosswalk: the 80 indicators of 2020 with the GII 2026 code and the status (same, renamed, redefined, dropped; their notes are in gii_profile.json's texts); new_2026: the 16 new indicators of the GII 2026 with their source, whether Puerto Rico data exist (yes, no, an FPR estimate possible, an FPR estimate given, proprietary, not verified) and n, the GII 2026 economies with data; for IN.3.3.2 (low-carbon energy use) pr_est holds FPR's estimate: the US EIA's consumption from nuclear, renewables and other as a % of Puerto Rico's total energy consumption, with its year, series, link and source, and no GII 2026 position; sources: the WIPO pages and files, with the date checked.
